title: Buying his first cornet for five dollars
summary: He buys a cornet from a neighbour of the curio shop and Chris Kelly shows him his first scale.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. Very tender. Let's see. Who started you off on the cornet? How did you get your first instrument?

Well I got the first instrument when I was working at the carolero store on Canelo Street. They had the King Dentist next door and there was a fellow, he was trying to learn the cornet. It was the cornet when I first played. And so he asked me if I wanted to buy it. So I told him no, I was playing the drum, which I always liked the horn instrument. And so he told me, he said, let me have it for five dollars. Somebody didn't have five dollars. He said, well all right, you take the horn. And he said, once and ever you got something, you paid it five dollars. So I got the horn, the cornet, and I went to Chris with the cornet. And for the first start, the sound of the horn, he rolled a piece of paper, put my mouth like you're going to spit and just sound the horn. And he wrote the first scale, a major scale, the horn, the half, the quart, the heat, and so forth.
I see. This guy next door to you when you were in the curio shop?
He didn't play at all. Just happened to have. He bought the horn. He pretended to play it, but he somehow or other didn't make no way with it, so he sold it to me for five dollars.
Yeah. That's to be Chris Wright Man, Banjo Man.
What's his full name? I just remember that.
Pratt, huh? This fellow which we call Sambo, his name is Edgar Joseph. You know him, huh? Yeah. Well that's really a relation to him. You call him and ask him, he'll tell you.
Well we'll get it from him.
Yeah, you can get it from him, sure.
